name: Genetic Non-Syndromic Renal or Urinary Tract Malformation
aliases: Isolated Congenital Anomalies of the Kidney and Urinary Tract

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Imaging Criteria for CAKUT Diagnosis

criteria.description: Presence of congenital structural abnormalities of the kidney or urinary tract confirmed by imaging
Identification of pathogenic variants in known CAKUT-associated genes
No clinical or laboratory evidence of syndromic involvement or extrarenal malformations
Positive family history of isolated renal or urinary tract malformations

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of congenital renal or urinary tract malformation on imaging with exclusion of syndromic features; genetic confirmation supportive but not mandatory.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis relies heavily on imaging and exclusion of syndromic causes; genetic testing may aid in confirmation.

pathognomonic.notes: Detected via prenatal or postnatal imaging
searchTerms: small or absent kidney at birth

common.notes: Recurrent infections common in affected children
May present as elevated serum creatinine
Obstruction at ureteropelvic junction or ureterovesical junction

occasional.notes: May develop in older children or adults
searchTerms: high blood pressure from kidney issues
blood pressure caused by kidney malformation

occasional.notes: May be related to urinary tract dysfunction
Due to enlarged or cystic kidneys

rare.notes: Kidney stones secondary to urinary stasis

rare.symptomName: Secondary anemia due to chronic kidney disease
searchTerms: anemia caused by chronic kidney disease
low red blood cells from kidney issues

laboratory: Elevated serum creatinine and blood urea nitrogen in renal impairment
Urine culture positive in urinary tract infections
imaging: Renal ultrasound showing hypoplasia, agenesis, or hydronephrosis
Magnetic resonance urography for detailed urinary tract anatomy
genetic: Pathogenic variants in genes such as PAX2, HNF1B, EYA1, and others associated with CAKUT
other: Family history consistent with autosomal dominant or recessive inheritance
Absence of extrarenal malformations or syndromic features

distinguishingFeatures: Onset after birth with no congenital abnormalities

redFlags: Severe bilateral renal agenesis or dysplasia
Progressive renal failure in infancy or early childhood
Recurrent febrile urinary tract infections with renal scarring
references: Sanna-Cherchi S, et al. Genetic basis of congenital anomalies of the kidney and urinary tract. Nat Rev Nephrol. 2018.
Orphanet: Genetic non-syndromic renal or urinary tract malformation (ORPHA:357506)
Nicolaou N, et al. Congenital anomalies of the kidney and urinary tract (CAKUT): clinical and molecular perspectives. Pediatr Nephrol. 2015.
